name: Presidente Juscelino Kubitschek International Airport
before:
Brasília's airport, 13 km from downtown in the Lago Sul administrative region, and the natural connecting point for anywhere in the Brazilian interior. It is run by Inframerica and shares some of its facilities with the Brasília Air Force Base.

Getting into the city is straightforward. Buses 102 and 102.1 run frequently to the main terminal at the Rodoviária, where travellers can pick up the metro or onward buses, and taxis wait at the terminal.

The airport's history is the city's history. When Juscelino Kubitschek first landed on the Central Plateau in 1956, Brasília was still only a plan, and the airfield that received the first crews of construction workers in October 1955 had a dirt runway and a terminal that was a cob-walled shack roofed with buriti leaves. It stood where the Integrated Bus and Train Terminal is today. Work on the permanent airport began in November 1956.

It was named after Kubitschek, Brazil's twenty first president, in April 1999.
after:
Brasília's airport, 13 km from downtown in the Lago Sul administrative region, and one of Brazil's main connecting hubs. It handled 16.7 million passengers in 2025. Inframerica has run it since 2012, and some facilities are shared with the Brasília Air Force Base. ANAC, the regulator, expects all of Inframerica's shares to be auctioned on 17 December 2026, under a renegotiated concession.

Getting into the city is straightforward. Buses 102 and 102.1 run to the Rodoviária bus station for the metro, and taxis wait outside arrivals.

The airport's history is the city's history. It opened on 3 May 1957, before the federal capital itself was founded, and took the name of President Juscelino Kubitschek in April 1999.

claims.claim: ANAC expects all of Inframerica's shares to be auctioned on 17 December 2026
claims.inAfter: ANAC, the regulator, expects all of Inframerica's shares to be auctioned on 17 December 2026, under a renegotiated concession.
claims.note: New: the brief asked who runs Brasília now. ANAC approved the tender and the contract amendment on 8 September 2026: the concession is being renegotiated through a settlement brokered by the TCU (the federal audit court), all of Inframerica's shares are to be sold in a competitive auction, and ANAC expects the auction on 17 December 2026. Infraero's 2025 report confirms the TCU settlement process, with an outcome expected in 2026. The date is ANAC's own, so the sentence names ANAC. A winner other than Inframerica's owners would take over the airport.

A expectativa é que o leilão ocorra no dia 17 de dezembro de 2026.
